title: Setup
subject: playwright-python
intro: Get Python, Playwright and the browsers installed, and run your first check that everything works.

steps.title: What you need
steps.body:
You need three things on your computer:

- **Python 3.10 or newer** from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
- **Git**, to download this course
- A code editor. **VS Code** with the Python extension works well.

Check Python with the command below. On macOS/Linux you may need `python3`.

steps.title: A virtual environment per project
steps.body:
A virtual environment (venv) is a private folder of packages for one project, so versions don't clash with other projects.

Create it once inside the course folder, then **activate** it every time you open a new terminal.
steps.code:
python -m venv venv

# Windows
venv\Scripts\activate

# macOS / Linux
source venv/bin/activate

steps.question: Why use a virtual environment?
options: It keeps this project's packages separate from other projects
Playwright refuses to install without one
steps.explain: A venv isolates packages per project. Playwright works without one, but a venv avoids version clashes.

steps.title: Install Playwright and the browsers
steps.body:
Two commands do it:

- `pip install -r core/subjects/playwright-python/requirements.txt` installs the Python packages, including **pytest-playwright**.
- `playwright install --with-deps` downloads Playwright's own builds of **Chromium, Firefox and WebKit**. `--with-deps` also installs system libraries the browsers need (mainly on Linux).

steps.prompt: Put the setup steps in order.
items: Create the venv: python -m venv venv
Run pytest to check it works
steps.explain: Packages go into the active venv, so activate it before pip install. Browsers are downloaded by the playwright command that pip installed.

steps.title: Run a smoke test
steps.body: Copy the exercise into `my-work/setup/` and complete it: open https://example.com and check the page title is **Example Domain**. If it passes, your setup works.

points: Python 3.10+, Git and an editor are all you need to start.
Create a venv once; activate it in every new terminal.
pip installs the packages; `playwright install --with-deps` downloads Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
A one-line smoke test proves the whole setup works.
notes.code:
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate   # Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r core/subjects/playwright-python/requirements.txt
playwright install --with-deps
notes.remember: No activated venv is the most common reason for 'module not found' errors.

steps.title: Where your code goes
steps.body:
Each module has a `lesson.json` (what you're reading now), starter files in `exercises/` and reference answers in `solutions/`.

You write your own code in `my-work/<module-id>/`, so the course files stay clean.

steps.question: You start the Locators exercises. Where do you write your code?
steps.explain: Copy the starter from exercises/ into my-work/locators/ and work there.

steps.title: Small steps, then notes
steps.body: Lessons come in short batches. After each batch you get **notes**: the key points and a code snippet. They are saved on the **Notes** page so you can revise any time.

points: Every batch ends with notes you can revise later.
notes.remember: Try the exercise first, then compare with solutions/.
